concepts.definition: F15 addresses release identification, publication, qualification, acceptance, selection and successor conservation. Its instance premises are recursive products, published cuts, mutable carriers, derived assets, external services and successor lines; these premises are additional to the commitments.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises, which the commitments do not supply, are
named in the rows as follows:

concepts.label: Release and successor conservation family

concepts.definition: Substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition are distinct lineage roles. Each binds its own identity and basis. Candidate source, release cut, release subject and version-line selector are also distinct generic release objects.

grounding.quote: substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product, install, artifact and product definition are distinct objects.
a candidate source, a release cut, a release subject and a version-line selector are distinct, and equal version text collapses none.

concepts.label: Product lineage and generic release objects

concepts.definition: A stable repository-local key assigned by Product release authority to one independently released source project.
concepts.label: Project Release Namespace

concepts.definition: The exact repository-relative source-project root and Git tree object selected for one cut.

grounding.quote:
- Project Subtree: the exact repository-relative source-project root and
  Git tree object selected for one cut;

concepts.label: Project Subtree

concepts.definition: Mutable source-project state constructing a possible successor.

grounding.quote:
- Candidate Source: the candidate source of FOUNDATIONS §2, the mutable
  source-project state constructing a possible successor;

concepts.label: Candidate Source

concepts.definition: Mutable project-qualified carrier for the current candidate window.

grounding.quote:
- RC Branch: a mutable project-qualified carrier for the current
  candidate window;

concepts.label: RC Branch

concepts.definition: An annotated project-qualified Git tag together with its exact Product release subject, naming one published candidate and, once accepted, one released Product; it realises a release cut.
concepts.label: Immutable RC Cut

concepts.definition: Mutable project-qualified tag alias naming the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for one project and version line; a discovery selector rather than a consumer's governing basis.
concepts.label: Version-Line Selector

concepts.definition: Optional mutable project-qualified convenience carrier aligned with the selector's latest-published commit.

grounding.quote:
- Release Branch: an optional mutable project-qualified convenience
  carrier aligned to the same latest-published commit as the selector.

concepts.label: Release Branch

concepts.definition: Three-phase process: mutable candidate construction; immutable RC publication with monotonic version-line advancement; exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption.
concepts.label: Release process

concepts.definition: Evaluation bound to an exact immutable cut, its release claims, governing basis, observation boundaries, evidence, owner verdicts, gaps and complete predecessor-successor relation.
concepts.label: Exact-cut qualification

concepts.definition: Separate explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs, verifies and pins a selected immutable RC. Its read-only Adoption Plan binds the current definition bytes and basis to exact target identities and emits a deterministic digest; fleet adoption uses one aggregate digest over all exact per-definition plans.

grounding.quote:
Adoption is a separate
explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs,
verifies and pins the selected immutable RC.

The read-only plan,
the Adoption Plan of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4, binds the current Product
Definition bytes and basis to the target immutable cut, annotated tag
object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, then emits a
deterministic plan digest.

concepts.label: Consumer adoption and Adoption Plan

concepts.definition: Optional release-scoped surfaces include release notes, release and installed-distribution manifests, dependency declarations, package or installed-carrier metadata, qualification receipts, and branch and tag identity declarations.
concepts.label: Release-scoped assets

concepts.definition: Declared exact Product member set or artifact constituting the release subject, distinguished from its describing claim surfaces, excluded mutable source fields and the wider repository carrier.

grounding.quote:
- the exact Product member set or artifact constituting the release
  subject;
- the release-scoped claim surfaces describing that subject; and
- co-located mutable source-project fields excluded from both.

concepts.label: Product release subject

conditions: A Product authority explicitly declares the relation when a source corpus and required distributed or derived assets need to remain usable as one versioned set.
concepts.definition: Cross-Product Release-Matched Asset Cohort naming every required Product and asset, exact source dependency, owning authorities, qualification boundary and publication transaction. The closed STDO stack cohort contains the standards corpus cut; distributed spec plugin and host assets carried by it; exact Axiom Indexer mechanics Product; exact STDO Representation Product; and its released a_c.STDO program and logical constraint map or equivalent semantic index, with complete source inventory, member digests, member-set digest and derivation cut identity.

grounding.quote:
A Product authority may declare an explicit cross-Product Release-Matched
Asset Cohort when one source corpus and its required distributed or
derived assets need to remain usable as one versioned set.

5. its released `a_c.STDO` axiomatic program and logical constraint map
   or equivalent semantic index, with the complete source-STDO member
   inventory, member digests, member-set digest and exact cut identity
   used to derive it.

concepts.label: Release-Matched Asset Cohort

conditions: Coordinated STDO cohort publication.
concepts.definition: Bounded construction using commit A for the exact STDO source cut and commit B for derived Products and index, followed by one atomic publication transaction. The separation avoids a same-commit self-reference because installed-manifest identity includes the annotated STDO tag object.

grounding.quote:
Exact installed-manifest identity includes the annotated STDO tag object,
so a same-commit carrier containing both that identity and derived child
bytes would be self-referential.

concepts.label: Two-commit construction and atomic publication

concepts.definition: Human Product authority's acceptance of the exact immutable RC identity, subject to mandatory qualification, review, scope, asset and gap gates. It is distinct from publication, selector movement, consumer adoption and operation outcomes.

grounding.quote: - the human Product authority accepted the exact immutable RC identity.

concepts.label: RC acceptance

concepts.definition: External backend, transport or operator-facing service outside the local carrier on which a release claim depends. It may remain outside Product for carrier and migration classification while still blocking the dependent claim.

grounding.quote:
Such a dependency may remain out of
Product for carrier and migration classification while still blocking the
dependent release claim

concepts.label: External qualification dependency

concepts.definition: A successor's claim about one affecting predecessor claim: conserved means retained; superseded means replaced by an accepted successor relation; intentionally removed means removed by current Product authority; not applicable means no successor effect with a bounded reason. These predicates are not result values. An unresolved disposition states no claim and has no result; evaluation of a stated disposition records a separate core result with its predicate.

grounding.quote:
An unresolved disposition states no claim and so has no result: in the
qualification of the affected claim it is a planned assessment without a
closed result

concepts.label: Successor claim disposition

concepts.definition: Provenance ledger recording this member's claimed treatment of rc.2 RELEASE_METHOD.md rows, their loci, generalisations and additions. Routes are provenance only; conserved rows are said to be restated in this member's own text. The ledger itself does not decide conservation.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row is restated in this member's own
text; a route is provenance only.

concepts.label: Release source disposition ledger

concepts.definition: Tier 2 particular method and process constitution owning method position and identity, constitutional chain and surfaces, manifesto and litmus tests, requirements and design law, trace closure, live-surface law, outcome conservation, change management, triage, classification, consistency and sprint boundaries, ambiguity, lifecycle sufficiency, lineage and release-version boundary, migration, procedures, design-record conventions and general build-tenant binding. Its mechanisms realise foundational principles and may be realised differently under those same principles.

grounding.quote:
nothing here is foundational, every clause
names the principle that requires it (P0 to P6, FOUNDATIONS §3), and each
mechanism could be realised differently under the same principles.

concepts.label: SPEC_METHOD

concepts.definition: Meta-constitutional process for building spec-driven projects: relates goals, intent, product, requirements, design, code, evidence and repricing; defines sufficiency, requirement truth kinds and iterative authority flow. It should bootstrap a new project process without the former implementation; together with surviving domain specification it can reconstruct the project.

grounding.quote:
If a project's implementation
disappears, the method should still be sufficient to bootstrap a new
spec-driven project process from scratch; the method plus the surviving domain specification
can reconstruct the project

concepts.label: Process constitution

conditions: Within urn:stdo:bounded-context:method-identity under the selected complete basis.
concepts.definition: STDO names four areas: S Specification owned by SPEC_METHOD; T Ticketing owned by TICKETS; D Design owned by DESIGN_MODULE; O Outcome-Driven Development, whose complete identity and realisation meaning are owned by ODD.

grounding.quote:
S,
Specification, owned by this member; T, Ticketing, owned by
[TICKETS](TICKETS.md); D, Design, owned by the design profile member
[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md); and O, Outcome-Driven Development, the
complete area whose identity and realisation meaning are owned by its
profile member [ODD](ODD.md).

concepts.label: STDO method identity

concepts.definition: F10 explains how specification governs realisations, using additional instance premises of owned layers, layered surfaces, several realisations and immutable releases. The source attributes recovered standing to P0; independent standing to P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6; derivation of P4b to P0 and P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts; and derivation of P5 to P0 and P6 with P0's open-world premise.

grounding.quote:
Standing of the commitments cited (FOUNDATIONS §3): P0
recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and
P2, with P0's premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable; P5
derived from P0 and P6, with P0's open-world premise.

concepts.label: Chain, outcome and build-tenant binding family

concepts.definition: Bounded work-wave surface naming current overriding concerns; more immediate than intent and higher-level than product definition and requirements. It keeps temporary focus out of deeper layers until intentionally repriced there.

grounding.quote:
The goals surface is the bounded work-wave surface: it captures the current
overriding concerns for the next body of work, keeps temporary focus out of
deeper constitutional layers until it is intentionally repriced there, and
is more immediate than intent while remaining higher-level than product
definition and requirements.

concepts.label: Goals

concepts.definition: Constitutional surface defining purpose and direction, why the system exists and which directional changes are in or out of scope.

grounding.quote:
Intent states why the
system exists and what directional change is in or out of scope;

concepts.label: Intent

concepts.definition: Present-tense definition of the mutable source project's current product realisation, key terms, boundaries and decomposable end-state shape. It bridges direction and obligation and routes to actual authority locations; it is neither the immutable release cut nor the installed product nor a rival truth surface.

grounding.quote:
It is not the immutable release cut
and not the installed product; those are the lineage objects of FOUNDATIONS
§2

concepts.label: Product Definition

concepts.definition: Full constitutional WHAT: invariant truths the project must make true, including capabilities, guarantees, constraints, governance and verification obligations; not merely user-visible features.

grounding.quote:
Requirements are the constitutional what of the project. They are not
limited to user-visible features: the live requirement surface may include
capabilities, invariants, constraints, governance and verification
obligations; what matters is that each requirement states something the
project must make true.

concepts.label: Requirements

concepts.definition: Structural HOW choosing decisions, interfaces, topology, carrier documents, placement, entry and control surfaces, runtime wiring, packaging and lawful tenant boundaries that satisfy requirements. ADRs are durable design records, not an additional constitutional layer.

grounding.quote:
Design
defines the structural decisions, interfaces, carrier surfaces and delivery
topology that make those truths achievable; ADRs are one durable form of
design record, not a second constitutional layer above design.

concepts.label: Design and ADRs

concepts.definition: Realisation implements declared decisions as software code, performed human procedure or both, according to its execution binding. The binding separates requirements calculus, computational calculus and execution environment; each tenant chooses its calculi and environment as design.

grounding.quote:
Code
realises those decisions where the selected execution environment is
software; a performed human procedure realises them where it is a human
process, and both where it is mixed (§11).
the division of a binding into requirements calculus, computational calculus and execution environment: a domain choice of this member; each tenant's calculus and environment: that tenant's design

concepts.label: Realisation and execution binding

concepts.definition: Homeostatic chain: Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis → Repricing at the layer named by the change class. Events retain what happened in the binding's carrier; projection reconstructs current truth where that record suffices; delta reveals intended-versus-realised drift; scenarios test operational meaning; gap analysis exposes model insufficiency.

grounding.quote:
Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code
  → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis
  → Repricing at the layer its change class names

concepts.label: Constitutional chain and feedback responsibilities

concepts.definition: Two independent declared-state axes for every live requirement family: Status is Active, Deferred, Superseded or Orphaned; Category is Capability, Constraint / Guarantee, Governance or Verification. Capability means required behaviour/function/surface; Constraint / Guarantee bounds behaviour by invariant/law/safety/portability/semantic guarantee; Governance controls lifecycle/authority/visibility/release/operator action; Verification concerns tests/evidence/traceability/qualification/forensic surfaces.

grounding.quote:
Every live requirement family is classified on two independent axes (P3,
P1; rc.2 #requirement-classification-rules): lifecycle status (Active,
Deferred, Superseded, Orphaned) and requirement category (the four above).

concepts.label: Requirement category and lifecycle status

concepts.definition: Operational lifecycle for any material product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin surface, public interface, data surface or capability: intent, requirement, build, assurance, release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry, retirement. Each phase has a declared state: answered; not applicable with reason; or unknown with a named Gap: or Unanswered: marker. These are not evaluation results.

grounding.quote:
Any material
product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin
surface, public interface, data surface or capability has an operational
lifecycle, whose canonical chain is intent, requirement, build, assurance,
release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry, retirement.

concepts.label: Operational lifecycle

conditions: Product-outcome-bearing work wave.
concepts.definition: One explicitly selected unresolved, directly verifiable product-defined outcome with a declared acceptance interval. Material advance is accepted material movement toward it and alone projects product progress; prerequisite readiness is bounded enabling work naming its obligation; preservation is useful repeated proof rather than progress; regression is not new progress and adds an affected-path promotion block.

grounding.quote:
Every product-outcome-bearing work wave identifies one explicitly selected,
unresolved, directly verifiable product-defined outcome and declares the
acceptance interval for that instance.

concepts.label: Selected product outcome and progress evidence

grounding.quote: release process is separate from live specification and owns neither Product meaning nor consumer adoption.
a refused, stopped or fail-closed release operation, an invalid state and a failed check report in the one core, and none is read as success.

constraints.statement: A mutable workspace has no fixed identity and is not called a Product. An install used as builder substrate is bound as a development product and transfers no meaning or authority to the authored Product; a product definition is a source-project surface, not the released artifact. Shared carriers, names and paths grant no membership. Release handling follows intake triage, and an open release window permits no untriaged change. Release process owns neither Product meaning nor adoption; operation outcome is not acceptance. Refusal, stopping, fail-closed operation, invalid state and failed checks report in the core and are never success.
constraints.uncertainty: The full lineage taxonomy, intake determinations and core result algebra are referenced outside the supplied excerpts.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: F15 traces but does not own FOUNDATIONS §2 lineage objects. Consequence standing comes from FOUNDATIONS §3. Ref forms, namespace pattern, root spelling, phases, publication steps, acceptance criteria and cohort mechanics are identified as added choices, not deductions alone; actual namespaces and cohort declarations belong to Product authority, cut acceptance to human Product authority, removal to current Product authority, and support-line mechanisms to the consumer. The family table accounts for §1–§9; open questions and source dispositions decide nothing. Consumers apply only their owning rule: the release-operation results paragraph has no external-member consumer; external-dependency and support-line rules have no separate consumer; installed-manifest bindings and manager result mappings do not acquire authority merely by resembling these rows.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced owners and consumer loci are described by this excerpt but their full bodies are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
Equal version text does not collapse these identities. Branches and the
version-line selector may move. An immutable RC tag never moves (P3).

constraints.statement: All seven release identities remain distinct despite equal version text. Branches and selector are movable; an immutable RC tag never moves.

conditions: Shared release source for the future-ref requirements.
exceptions: The declared single-project unqualified profile and preserved historical refs have the separately stated conditions.

grounding.quote:
`<project>` is one explicit Project Release Namespace. It matches
`[a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*`, contains no slash, is unique within the
release source, and remains stable for the continuing release line.

RC branch:              refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>
immutable RC cut tag:   refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>
version-line selector:  refs/tags/<project>/v<version>
release branch:         refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>

constraints.statement: The authority-assigned namespace matches [a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*, has no slash, is release-source unique and remains stable on a continuing line. Directory/display/definition/package names and matching versions cannot infer or reassign it. Shared future publications use refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>, refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>, refs/tags/<project>/v<version>, and optional refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>; future unqualified cuts/selectors are prohibited. Specification Stack allocates specification_methodology, axiom_indexer and stdo_representation; these distinguish refs without merging Products or implying dependency/composition.
constraints.uncertainty: The separately supplied naming section also permits alternative spelling under a proven collision-free ref policy; the interaction with 'exact ref shapes' is retained as a residual.

conditions: An immutable cut in a shared release source.
exceptions: The repository root is spelled '.' and its subtree tree equals the repository-root tree.
constraints.statement: The cut binds all seven listed identity components: namespace/owner; qualified ref/annotated tag object; peeled commit/root tree; normalised subtree root at that commit; exact subtree tree; member inventory/claim bytes; predecessor/successor dispositions. A subtree root is a locator, not Product identity: slash-separated Git path, no leading/trailing slash or empty, '.' or '..' component, except '.' alone for repository root; each other component is the exact traversed tree-entry bytes. Moving the project changes locator and cut identity without reassigning namespace. A monorepo tag admits no sibling members; unrelated sibling bytes stay outside the subject. Inventory or payload digest without qualified ref, commit, subtree root and subtree tree is not a complete reacquirable identity.

conditions: Project qualification or a version line spanning its transition.
exceptions: An additional archival ref may preserve reachability to the same historical tag object.

grounding.quote:
Project qualification is prospective. Existing unqualified refs retain
their names, objects, peels and public links.

The historical unqualified selector is preserved at
its existing object and ceases to be the current selector for the shared
source; it is not force-moved to imitate the qualified namespace (P3).

constraints.statement: Qualification is prospective. Existing unqualified ref names, objects, peels and public links remain; historical tags cannot be recreated, re-annotated, moved or replaced. Product-local cut names and logical release URIs remain unchanged, including stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/; transport namespace is not inserted into that URI. Resolution binds the logical cut to an exact historical or qualified ref and fails closed if a project-local coordinate names different tag objects. Latest is the greatest positive RC ordinal across the project's historical and qualified cuts. First qualified publication creates the qualified selector; the old selector stays at its existing object and ceases to be current.

grounding.quote:
There is no second final cut after an accepted RC. Publication immediately
makes the new highest ordinal discoverable through the version-line
selector; acceptance remains a verdict over the exact immutable RC rather
than a second carrier.

constraints.statement: Publication immediately exposes the new highest ordinal through the selector. Acceptance is a verdict on that immutable RC, with no second final cut/carrier. Any changed byte capable of affecting Product or a release-scoped claim requires publication and review of a higher immutable RC.

conditions: Before RC publication or during candidate construction.

grounding.quote:
The intended Product boundary, release-scoped claims, excluded
source-project state and qualification basis become explicit before RC
publication. A material scope change is repriced instead of being silently
absorbed

constraints.statement: Make intended Product boundary, release claims, excluded source state and qualification basis explicit before publication. Reprice material scope changes; do not silently absorb them. Mutable candidate source remains non-operative for released consumers.

conditions: Publishing an RC cut.
exceptions: Atomic transport push in this general publication procedure is required where the transport supports it; coordinated cohorts impose a stronger atomic-or-refuse rule.

grounding.quote:
8. atomically pushes the carrier, RC branch, immutable RC tag, selector
   and optional release branch where the transport supports it;
9. verifies remotely that the immutable tag, selector and release branch
   resolve to the highest published RC commit; and
10. records enough ref, subtree, identity and inventory evidence to
    reacquire the cut without trusting a mutable checkout.

constraints.statement: In order: confirm triaged scope and lawful constitutional re-entry; declare exact subject and claims; reconcile release notes and release-facing assets; run proportionate pre-RC qualification and operator checks; commit exact carrier; resolve and record namespace/subtree root/tree; in shared sources create annotated immutable <project>/v<version>-rc.<n> and annotated selector <project>/v<version> over that commit; push carrier, RC branch, cut, selector and optional release branch atomically where supported; remotely verify alignment with the highest published RC commit; retain reacquisition evidence independent of mutable checkout. Published tags are immutable. Further work increments n on the same version line when that line remains applicable; bounded review repair alone requires no minor increment. A higher published RC without matching selector advancement is invalid and fail-closed and never permits treating the older cut as latest.

exceptions: Artifact presence can establish a claim whose exact predicate is presence.

grounding.quote:
Evidence matches the claim. Source success does not prove packaged or
installed behaviour; packaging equivalence does not prove semantic
behaviour; artifact presence does not prove usability unless presence is
the exact claim

constraints.statement: Qualification binds namespace, qualified immutable ref, annotated tag object, peeled commit, repository tree, subtree root/tree, declared members, exact claim bytes, governing Product/release basis, each property and observation boundary, evidence subjects, owner verdicts, gaps and complete declared predecessor relation. Evidence must match the claim: source success proves neither packaged nor installed behaviour; packaging equivalence does not prove semantic behaviour; presence does not prove usability. Acceptance requires completed exact-cut review and required operator checks plus human acceptance of that exact subject. A qualifying-byte change leaves the verdict attached to the old cut and requires a higher RC; acceptance does not move or rewrite the selector or create a final carrier.

conditions: Advancing one project's version line.
exceptions: Release-branch preparation applies only when that optional carrier is used; general transport atomicity is conditional on transport support.

grounding.quote:
Advancement is refused when the target has no matching immutable annotated
RC tag, any higher ordinal already exists, the selector would move to a
lower RC, or the selector and release branch would not align to the same
highest commit (P5).

constraints.statement: Identify exact new tag, ordinal and peeled commit; confirm no higher ordinal exists; confirm selector absent or at a lower ordinal on that same project line; atomically create/force-update the annotated selector to the new highest commit; align optional release branch; atomically push carrier, RC branch, immutable tag, selector and optional release branch where supported; remotely verify highest-commit selector peel and matching immutable annotated tag. Refuse missing matching annotated cut, any already higher ordinal, downward move, or selector/release-branch misalignment. Forward movement is strictly increasing by ordinal; repair defects through higher cuts, never old-tag movement or selector rollback. Selector means v<version>-rc.latest; concrete cuts remain addressable.

conditions: Channel resolution or adoption.
exceptions: Intentional retention of an older cut uses its explicit immutable URI and digest with exact-basis operations such as sync, not the latest channel.

grounding.quote:
Channel adoption also refuses a same-line target whose ordinal
is below the Product Definition's current exact basis.

Resolution requires an
annotated selector with a distinct peeled commit; absence of a peeled
selector ref fails closed and cannot be interpreted as a lightweight
selector whose tag object is its commit

constraints.statement: Selector answers only which highest published cut exists, never which cut governs a consumer. A Product Definition may retain stdo://channels/<version> for discovery, but operative basis is exact stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/ plus installed-manifest digest; moving the selector updates no consumer. Resolution enumerates namespace cuts, including preserved unqualified historical cuts during transition, chooses greatest positive ordinal, and requires annotated cut and selector peeling to the same commit. Missing peeled selector, lagging/elsewhere selector or same-line adoption below current exact basis fails closed/refuses as specified; missing peel is never reinterpreted as lightweight-selector success.

conditions: Mutation of one Product Definition or a fleet.

grounding.quote:
Mutation requires that exact digest as the
operator's acceptance and re-derives it before changing any Product
Definition. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates the
acceptance.

constraints.statement: Presentation and mutation are separate invocations. Mutation requires operator acceptance of the exact deterministic presented plan digest and re-derives it before changing any definition. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates acceptance. Fleet mutation requires an aggregate digest over every exact per-definition plan. Planning inside a mutating invocation is not external presentation and cannot authorise itself. Plan hashing and manager command boundaries are owned by PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4.
constraints.uncertainty: The hashing algorithm and complete manager command contract are not supplied.

conditions: A release-scoped surface is used.

grounding.quote:
Before RC publication, each used surface is reconciled to the exact RC
subject. After publication, changing one of those bytes creates a
different candidate and therefore requires a higher RC tag. The
version-line selector has no content-reconciliation phase because it adds
no new Product bytes (P3).

constraints.statement: Reconcile each used surface to the exact RC before publication. Changing its bytes afterward creates a different candidate and needs a higher RC. Selector adds no Product bytes and has no reconciliation phase. Exact version/RC identity belongs in release carriers and consumer basis bindings; live constitutional version-label use follows SPEC_METHOD's specification surface rule.

grounding.quote:
Once the immutable RC is published, no post-review
carrier delta is admitted into that cut. Publication-caused ticket or
source-work bookkeeping is recorded afterward on the continuing source
branch and cannot move the immutable RC tag

constraints.statement: Before qualification declare namespace, exact subtree root, exact Product members/artifact, describing release-claim surfaces and co-located mutable fields excluded from both. Commit co-location confers no Product membership; subtree tree and member inventory distinguish subject from wider carrier. After publication admit no post-review carrier delta into the cut. Record publication-caused ticket/source bookkeeping later on the continuing source branch without moving the immutable tag.

conditions: A cohort is declared.
exceptions: Only the leading v cut-name marker is normalised for version comparison.

grounding.quote:
Qualification normalises only that leading cut-name marker
and requires exact suffix equality. Equal versions establish release
matching only.

constraints.statement: Co-location, equal version or common actor cannot infer a cohort. Every required member uses exactly <version>-rc.<n>; local cuts/refs render v<version>-rc.<n>, embedded asset fields omit v. Matching collapses no Product identity, inventory, tag, acceptance judgment or release authority. Missing, stale, differently versioned, wrong-source-cut or non-reproducible source-member/digest closure makes a cohort incomplete. Changing any indexed source member invalidates the old derived candidate for the successor; regenerate, mechanically validate, independently qualify where required, and release the index under the same new cut name. A stale index may persist as immutable history but cannot accompany changed source as current cohort.

conditions: Coordinated STDO cohort publication.

grounding.quote:
7. a mandatory post-tag, pre-push gate re-runs qualification over every
   local annotated tag object and peel, selector, RC and release branch,
   normalised version mapping, target commit and the exact closed ref
   set; it also fetches and binds the expected remote object ID or
   required absence for every destination ref; and
8. one transport transaction atomically publishes only that qualified
   carrier branch and complete Product ref set.

constraints.statement: In order: commit A freezes exact corpus, plugin, release record and qualification bytes; create its annotated STDO tag locally without push; install and verify that exact cut to obtain manifest identity for every derived Product/index; derive and freeze Axiom Indexer, STDO Representation, semantic index and cohort record in commit B; qualify B against the exact local STDO tag before child tags; prepare annotated child tags and every local RC branch, selector and optional release branch; mandatory post-tag/pre-push qualification covers every local annotated object/peel, selector, RC/release branch, normalised version, target commit and exact closed ref set, and fetches expected remote OID or required absence for every destination; atomically publish only that qualified carrier branch and complete Product ref set.

conditions: Publishing or remotely verifying a coordinated cohort.

grounding.quote:
If the remote does not support atomic ref publication, publication
refuses. The process has no sequential-push fallback.

constraints.statement: Refuse non-atomic remote publication with no sequential fallback. Every immutable tag is create-only with bound remote absence; every mutable carrier, RC branch, selector and release branch has its own compare-and-swap lease, e.g. --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected-oid>, in the same transaction. Missing expected ref, unexpected existing tag or changed OID stops publication; refetch and repeat complete content and local-ref-graph qualification before another push. Lease mismatch permits no unguarded force, partial push or in-place expectation update. Remote verification fails closed for missing, lightweight, wrong-version or wrong-Product-commit required refs, or selectors/release branches not matching cuts. Later bookkeeping cannot move immutable cohort tags.
constraints.uncertainty: The phrase 'lightweight' is retained as applied by the source to required cohort refs; its precise tag-versus-branch checking scope is not separately defined here.

conditions: Qualifying a coordinated cohort.

grounding.quote:
Post-publication qualification verifies the same relation from remote refs
and refuses a partial cohort

constraints.statement: Content qualification binds commit-A tag/manifest, commit-B source tree, every Product-local target ref, version marker, member inventory, semantic-index bytes and complete source digest closure, establishing taggability without qualifying-byte change. After tags and mutable refs exist, local-ref-graph qualification binds annotated objects, peels, commits, exact push set and all fetched remote expectations/absences to unchanged content results. Post-publication qualification verifies the same relation remotely and refuses partial cohorts. Adding/changing cohort law changes qualifying bytes: it governs only a higher immutable RC containing them and cannot retroactively make an earlier cut a coordinated cohort.

conditions: Considering RC acceptance.
exceptions: Independent exact-cut review is required where applicable; blocking gaps may instead be addressed by explicitly narrowing claimed scope.

grounding.quote:
Each criterion is a mandatory gate in the sense of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse):
it applies irrespective of any selection of checks after a change, and
retained evidence satisfies it only under the validity conditions stated
there

constraints.statement: An RC may be accepted when pre-RC qualification passed for its subject; required independent exact-cut review passed; required operator review completed; scope and successor relation are stable; assets accurately describe the cut; all release-blocking gaps, including promotion-blocking findings under EVALUATION §5, are closed or scope explicitly narrowed; and human Product authority accepted that exact identity. Every criterion remains applicable regardless of check selection after change; retained evidence counts only under referenced validity conditions. Acceptance attaches to the cut and neither advances nor rolls back the selector. Adoption separately evaluates the latest exact channel target and mutates only after acceptance of its digest-bound plan.
constraints.uncertainty: The external evidence-reuse conditions and full promotion-blocking finding criteria are not supplied.

conditions: A claim depends on an external service.

grounding.quote:
A clean skip caused by an unhealthy external dependency is an evaluation
not performed, which has no result

constraints.statement: An unhealthy-dependency clean skip is Not performed and has no evaluation result. It may preserve correct Product classification but establishes no passing dependent capability. Before acceptance, qualify against a healthy dependency or narrow the claim; being out of Product does not remove the claim's dependency.

conditions: A candidate evolves a predecessor release.

grounding.quote:
A successor identifies the exact predecessor immutable RC whose semantic
claims it evolves. That origin remains immutable for the candidate. Every
predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor receives one semantic
disposition

constraints.statement: Name one exact immutable predecessor and keep that origin immutable for the candidate. Give every predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor one semantic disposition, evaluated on evidence. Reuse an earlier conserved reading only if owning text and consumer bindings are unchanged or shown unaffected. Unresolved disposition blocks the affected claim's qualification and is a planned assessment without closed result, not falsity. Patch absence does not prove loss if successor-native behaviour survives; naming/code similarity does not prove conservation. Compare the same material case, scope and authority, required/permitted/prohibited behaviour, absent triggers/exceptions/prerequisites, owning text and consumer bindings, including counterexamples. Indicative wording can bind; replacing must/shall alone proves neither conservation nor supersession. Obligations, preferences, every exception and scope condition must retain their meaning or the claim is not conserved. Package-wide wording equivalence proves no claim. Conserved records predating this test must be reevaluated before qualification and remain unresolved meanwhile. Recorded dispositions establish nothing until evaluated and are distinct from owner acceptance dispositions.

conditions: Maintenance or support lines may affect retained claims.

grounding.quote:
Where a maintenance or support line may affect retained claims, the
release basis identifies the watched source, observation boundary,
inclusion policy and successor candidate. Relevant changes receive
semantic disposition at material integration and exact-cut qualification.
The consumer owns its record, branch strategy, comparison and proof
mechanism

constraints.statement: Release basis names watched source, observation boundary, inclusion policy and successor candidate. Relevant changes receive semantic dispositions at both material integration and exact-cut qualification. Consumer owns record, branch strategy, comparison and proof mechanism. EVALUATION §5 separately owns acceptance requirements for the disposition record.
constraints.uncertainty: Full external acceptance requirements are not supplied; the family table reports that unresolved dispositions block acceptance.

grounding.quote:
"must remain usable as one versioned set" is written "need to
remain usable", the condition of declaration and not a new obligation;

it
decides nothing beyond the rules it names.

constraints.statement: The ledger claims conservation for all listed predecessor anchors from release-publication-context and position through open-questions, routing each to its corresponding current section, with generic objects at FOUNDATIONS §2, claim law at EVALUATION §1, adoption object/hashing/commands at PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4, and acceptance at EVALUATION §5. Recorded generalisations remove identity-name emphasis, replace 'this method' with §9 and 'Release Method bytes' with this member's bytes, use British spelling, and express 'need to remain usable' as declaration condition rather than a new obligation. New items are the family table, Results paragraph and claim/evaluation reading of successor dispositions; clean skip applies existing Results law without adding a rule. Family tables distinguish derived consequences from owned added choices and decide nothing beyond named rules.
constraints.uncertainty: These are authored provenance/conservation claims, not independently verified findings about the absent predecessor.

grounding.quote:
Routes are
provenance only; nothing here depends on that cut to be applied.

constraints.statement: SPEC_METHOD realises FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION and claims no foundational status; clauses name P0–P6 principles. PRODUCT_DEFINITION owns project binding, ASSURANCE testing law, TICKETS work carriers and RELEASE release mechanics. rc.2 #anchor routes into stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md; rc.2 MEMBER #anchor routes into that member of the same cut. Routes are provenance, not applicability dependencies.
constraints.uncertainty: Full imported laws are unavailable in this bounded source.

grounding.quote:
Its
overriding bias is declarative rather than imperative: the system should
primarily declare truths, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence
surfaces, and let lawful processing derive and realise work from that
declared surface.
Imperative procedure still exists and is subordinate to declared authority

constraints.statement: Specification is constitutional source, enabling re-derivation, audit and correction under explicit authority. The system should primarily declare truth, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence, letting lawful processing derive work; imperative procedure remains subordinate. Constitutional examples use neutral capability and authority identities to demonstrate capability; consumer particulars cannot become method precedent or law.
constraints.uncertainty: The examples claim is attributed to predecessor compressions rather than an rc.2 body; those compressions and PROFILES §1 are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
The authoritative split is strict: the surfaces bound as WHAT define WHAT;
design and realisation surfaces define HOW; no build tenant, design, code,
definition overlay or derived surface becomes co-equal constitutional
authority with the bound WHAT (P6).

constraints.statement: Method owns process constitution; conventional GOALS.md names current concerns, INTENT.md domain direction, PRODUCT.md mutable source-project definition, specification/requirements/ live derived requirements, and shared/tenant-local design chooses mechanism. Product definition binds actual authority locations and tenant registry locates project-owned realisations beneath one shared specification. Conventional names require no file moves or duplication. Bound WHAT alone defines WHAT; design/realisation define HOW; tenants, design, code, overlays and derived surfaces never become co-equal constitutional authority.

grounding.quote:
The expansion does not make the four owning
members independently selectable and does not reduce the released product
to four members: consumer authority remains one complete immutable released
cut with its exact member inventory

constraints.statement: The four-letter expansion neither permits independent selection of its owning members nor reduces the released Product to four members. Consumer authority remains one complete immutable released cut and exact member inventory.

exceptions: Blocking/escalation policy follows declared risk appetite except hard-stop prerequisite failures.

grounding.quote:
The lifecycle is a governed disambiguation pipeline: each major
boundary reduces the space of lawful interpretations and surfaces major
ambiguity explicitly; detection is mandatory; blocking or escalation is
policy under declared risk appetite, except for hard-stop prerequisite
failures

constraints.statement: The canonical statement compresses owning sections without independent authority. Every product publishes a layout-neutral routing definition locating constitution, local constitutional decisions, collective reference-frame bases, WHAT, independent tenant HOWs, work and explicit composition. Material terms resolve only with bounded context, owner, selected basis and scope; spelling alone creates no cross-context meaning/authority, and zero or multiple applicable meanings fail closed; seams require explicit imports/translations/equivalences/disambiguations. Major boundaries reduce lawful interpretations and expose ambiguity; detection is mandatory, blocking/escalation policy is qualified as stated. Products and runtime implementations cannot substitute for constitutional documents; capability claims needing end-to-end proof use scenarios. Sprints price proof cost and force close review as execution batches, never authority layers or concealment of drift.
constraints.uncertainty: Full resolution, hard-stop, scenario and sprint rules lie outside the supplied portions.

conditions: Applicable owned-layer, layered-surface, several-realisation or immutable-release premises of the corresponding F10 row.
exceptions: Negative proof is included where drift is plausible; the design-profile transform guidance has should force and applies only to governed boundaries.

grounding.quote: the steps of a construction, what its data means and how it is carried out are separately declared, so they stay three separate accounts across the binding.

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: F10 attributes authority to declared specification, trace ownership, derivable layers, immutable history, recorded gaps, selected outcomes, evidence-backed closure, distinct lineage and bounded terms. Realisation closure evidence includes authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift is plausible and remaining open pressure. Reusable method change retains one authority relation from evidence to realising consumer. Executor kind alone accepts/rejects nothing; human performance is not adjudication; structural validation is not correct execution; convenience weakens no obligation. Only its owner may weaken an obligation, through WHAT change. Each binding identifies operations, outcome values mapped into the core, and resource measures with units/boundaries; calculus applies wherever its declared laws hold regardless of executor. Project law owns multi-tenant development mechanics. Construction steps, data meaning and execution remain three accounts; mappings state and discharge preservation under ACTIVATION refinement and AC-013 where recorded in a_c. Chain order, categories/statuses, ADR conventions, adoption chain, binding divisions and resource choices are owned additions, not unqualified deductions. Consumers decide nothing beyond owning sections; canonical statement and source dispositions decide nothing independently.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed §6, §9–§11, foundational laws, adoption chain, ADR lifecycle and mapping discharge mechanisms are referenced but not supplied.

exceptions: Projection need not replay a complete event stream when the retained record is sufficient for Product obligations.

grounding.quote:
Load-bearing means owned, not software: the links
Code, Events and Projection name responsibilities every realisation
carries in the carrier its binding selects (§11), and no product owes a
code base or an event store that its binding does not select

constraints.statement: Every chain link must be owned. Goals lacking downstream repricing, unowned requirements, ungrounded design or code without design create accidental law. Code, Events and Projection are responsibilities in the selected carrier, not mandates for a codebase/event store. Events may use stream, ledger, signed record or observation log; projection depends on record sufficiency. Gap-driven constitutional repricing re-enters at the layer named by change class, generates goals/intent when wave/direction/scope changes, and updates affected layers. Requirements may mandate delivery surfaces, while design chooses their location/mechanism unless the path itself is constitutional.
constraints.uncertainty: The full change-class mapping and execution-binding rules are not supplied.

exceptions: Transitional paths may remain when explicitly retained as compatibility features.

grounding.quote:
It treats derived artifacts,
indexes, trace matrices, reports, automation and generated views, as read
models, never as constitutional truth. If these claims do not hold, the
work is not spec-driven.

constraints.statement: Define current goals before repricing deeper layers; intent before implementation; explicit present-tense product definition before requirements; and the full WHAT rather than a feature list. Prefer declared truth/boundaries over imperative procedure. Design explicitly bridges requirements to code, which must be derivable from both rather than justified by precedent. Major gates reduce interpretation space before downstream realisation. Claims require evidence through scenarios, tests, events, projection and delta; constitutional gaps require specification repricing. Keep authority directional during iteration and live surfaces present tense; erase superseded transition paths unless explicitly retained compatibility. Derived artifacts, indexes, matrices, reports, automation and generated views remain read models, never constitutional truth. Failure of these commitments means the work is not spec-driven.

conditions: Any one listed disqualifier holds.

grounding.quote: The work is not spec-driven if any of these holds

constraints.statement: Work is not spec-driven if a competent team cannot derive conformant intent from goals, product definition from intent, requirements from product definition, design from requirements, or code from requirements plus design; a live requirement lacks explicit status, category or design owner; lacks realisation or explicit deferment; code lacks requirement/design authority; a live constitutional domain artifact is rewritten in place; a capability lacks operational evidence; drift triaged to constitutional source leaves that source unrepriced; major boundary ambiguity is neither recorded nor explicitly governed; or a material product/module/function/application/runtime/capability has neither lifecycle signal nor recorded gaps for unanswered release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement questions.

conditions: Assessing reconstruction sufficiency for the selected span.
exceptions: Different conformant designs and codebases are possible; a local selected function's span excludes recreating the whole Product.

grounding.quote:
sufficiency is not
determinism, that a boundary crossed only by hiding a major ambiguity is not
sufficient, and that an accepted relation may be reused on its exact basis
after checking applicability and invalidation

constraints.statement: Specification-drivenness requires ordered reconstructability: competent teams should derive conformant intent, product definition, requirements, design and code from the appropriate upstream layer(s). Sufficiency is not determinism and cannot hide major ambiguity. Boundary failure is an upper-layer specification defect: goals may be unclear/contradictory/insufficiently concrete; intent vague/contradictory/insufficiently concrete; product underspecified/contradictory/nondecomposable; requirements underspecified/contradictory/polluted by accidental implementation detail; design incomplete/ambiguous/nonoperational for code derivation. ADRs/design documents are load-bearing. Accepted relations may be reused only on exact basis after applicability/invalidation checks. Ambiguity governance applies. The litmus neither waives the design profile's material-change gate nor demands rebuilding unchanged accepted views.
constraints.uncertainty: Full EVALUATION layered-sufficiency and DESIGN_MODULE coverage/reuse rules are not supplied.

conditions: Real use cases expose a gap.
exceptions: A merely missing implementation is not by itself constitutional insufficiency.

grounding.quote:
a gap becomes
intent only once it is concrete. Ad hoc coding pressure does not generate
intent; explicit gap analysis does.

constraints.statement: Scenario, deployment or external-review use cases feed current specification through explicit gap analysis. A constitutional gap re-enters the layer named by its change class and flows forward through that class's affected layers; write new goals/intent when wave, direction or scope changes. New intent arises from concrete repeated real-use pressure, not abstraction or ad hoc coding pressure. Iteration cumulatively refines requirements/design and re-derives code; implementation/testing/replay/scenario gaps feed repricing. Authority direction remains goals→intent→product→requirements→design, with requirements plus design governing code throughout.

exceptions: Intent may carry realisation detail when that detail is itself constitutional; lifecycle signal is required where materially relevant.

grounding.quote:
Requirements state stable obligations
that must be true; they carry explicit acceptance criteria and remain
sufficient for downstream design derivation

Before a downstream specification artifact is treated as complete, the
whole affected span is checked:

constraints.statement: Goals orient a wave and do not replace requirements. Intent carries no optional implementation detail absent constitutional necessity. Product bridges intent to obligations, is not release notes, and provides material use/install/release/live-use/observability/retirement signal. Requirements carry stable obligations, explicit acceptance criteria, derivability and material lifecycle obligations or named ambiguity gaps. Design selects HOW; ADRs are not another requirement surface. Live constitutional law uses present tense; remove, supersede or move dead law to commentary, including during migration. State current truth and affected boundary; version labels are for immutable release facts, selectors or clearly historical/superseded material, never mere recency branding. Before treating a downstream artifact as complete, check whole affected span for clear class, lawful re-entry, downstream derivability and agreement of active intent/product/requirements/design/qualification; otherwise the gate remains open.

exceptions: An upstream constitutional constraint may fix stack, carrier, runtime, filename, placement or packaging.

grounding.quote:
If a technology stack,
carrier or runtime is not already constrained by an upstream constitutional
surface, choosing it is part of design, not a separate upstream authority

constraints.statement: Requirements specify necessary control/delivery surfaces; design chooses mechanisms and declares tenant stack/human/mixed execution binding. Requirements may require authoritative bootstrap/control surfaces, bare axioms and canonical-method routing, while design chooses entry documents, embedded blocks, compiled artifacts or another lawful topology. Hardcoding filenames/placement absent constitutional necessity wrongly absorbs design detail and impedes re-derivation.
constraints.uncertainty: PRODUCT_DEFINITION §12's full lawful-topology constraints are not supplied.

conditions: A realisation boundary is governed by the tier-3 DESIGN_MODULE profile under its own adoption rule.
exceptions: Specific language, elimination of all imperative code, monadic/category vocabulary and replacing every exception with custom algebraic types are not required.

grounding.quote:
semantic
steps should read as transforms over admitted truth; effects should be
explicit and pushed to the edge.

Where a boundary composes
higher-order functions or effectful computation, it does require an
explicit composition and effect algebra with its applicable identity,
closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws

constraints.statement: Semantic steps should read as transforms over admitted truth and effects should be explicit at the edge. Needing orchestration, mutable workspace, service methods or defaults to discover meaning signals excessive imperative coupling. Implementation must remain readable, modular and honest about meaning/effects. A boundary composing higher-order or effectful computation requires explicit composition/effect algebra with applicable identity, closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws. Vocabulary is optional; this algebraic obligation is not.
constraints.uncertainty: Profile adoption and detailed composition laws are referenced externally.

conditions: Every live requirement family; every inherited or legacy requirement for legacy classification.
exceptions: Concrete paths, filenames and packaging belong in requirements only when constitutional.

grounding.quote:
A live requirement
is incomplete if either axis is missing. In project documents the
classification is explicit in the requirement's header metadata: `Status`
carries lifecycle status and `Category` carries the kind.

constraints.statement: Classify every live family by both independent axes, explicitly in Status and Category header metadata; missing either makes it incomplete. Categories remain constitutional truth kinds, not priority or user-facing labels. Not every requirement should become a marketed feature; avoid premature implementation freezing. Classify all inherited/legacy requirements: Deferred retains a not-yet-operative/realised obligation with honest deferment, never current closure; Superseded moves ownership and requires Implements and Supersedes in governing design; Active remains live law and needs an owning design decision written/updated; Orphaned is outside intended system and must be removed or explicitly superseded. Nothing live remains unclassified.

grounding.quote:
a requirement marked Active, or evidence classed as material advance,
cannot stand in for a `satisfied` result, and a requirement marked
Deferred or Orphaned cannot stand in for a `falsified` one

constraints.statement: Statuses, categories and legacy classes map to no core result. The same applies to evidence kinds, migration old-path classes, inherited-material adopted/superseded/deferred/orphaned, implementation carry_across/redundant/rewrite, ADR statuses and change classes. Evaluations reading them return their own predicate-bound core results; declared states are never combined as results. Legacy classification concerns standing in a project's live surface, whereas RELEASE §9 evaluates treatment of predecessor claims. For a successor, every affecting predecessor claim needs that separate disposition: Active can accompany semantic supersession; Superseded alone names no accepted successor relation; Orphaned is not intentional removal.
constraints.uncertainty: Several named classification systems are referenced without their complete definitions.

exceptions: Explicit honest deferment is an allowed alternative to realised downstream closure.

grounding.quote:
No hidden product
surface is allowed; behaviour without trace authority is accidental law
even if it works

constraints.statement: Every live requirement family maps to one or more design owners; every ADR/design record grounds itself with an explicit Implements: line. Every live requirement has downstream design/code/test closure or recorded honest deferment. Shipping code and tests must trace to live requirements and authorising design; hidden/working-but-unauthorised behaviour is accidental law. Unowned requirements, ungrounded designs, unrecorded deferment and code without owners signal design drift; tests asserting implementation habit lock it in. Persistent event/projection delta goes through intake diagnosis of code, requirement/design stack, predictive model or observation. Capability without scenario has unverified operational meaning. Feature treatment of guarantee/governance/verification is misclassification; in-place constitutional correction corrupts history. A use-case gap outside current requirements requires class-directed Requirements-or-upstream re-entry, not a code hack.

conditions: A domain artifact has been published as a live constitutional surface.
exceptions: Engine code, design, tests and tooling remain aggressively refactorable while mutable implementation surfaces; explicitly retained responsibilities must satisfy §7's retention relation.

grounding.quote:
Live domain artifacts, once published as live
constitutional surfaces, are immutable in place; if one is wrong, the valid
actions are to supersede it with a new version or to withdraw or delete it
from the live surface.

constraints.statement: Live surfaces are versioned constitutional history, possibly multiple over time, never scratch space. Correct them only by superseding, withdrawing or deleting from live use, never silent in-place mutation. Retire superseded transitions, migration scaffolds and fallbacks; retained responsibilities require the referenced retention relation. Preserve past through version control, operational event history where present and superseded artifacts. No perpetual compatibility-shim requirement is created.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced §7 closure criterion and retention relation are not supplied.

conditions: A lifecycle phase materially affects the designed thing or its obligations.
exceptions: Not applicable is allowed with a stated reason; deferment requires naming the deferment and future owning surface; implementation mechanism need not be prescribed for every phase.

grounding.quote: Silent absence is not a valid lifecycle answer.

constraints.statement: Product definition and requirements provide sufficient constitutional lifecycle signal for downstream design or explicitly record ambiguity. Product names boundary, use context and material release/install/live-use/observability/retirement posture; requirements state invariant build, assurance, release, deployment, usage, telemetry, retirement, ownership, source-truth, authority and interpretation obligations. Every phase is answered, reasoned not applicable, or a named unknown gap; silence is invalid. This detects ambiguity rather than requiring every requirement to be a release plan. Missing signal cannot be filled by local convention, implementation precedent, prompt prose or test fixture; reprice the proper constitutional surface or record governed debt. Phase states map to no core result; answered/not-applicable never substitutes for satisfied, and evaluations must return their own predicate-bound results.

conditions: Product-outcome-bearing work wave.
exceptions: Acceptance exhausts only the bound instance and interval, not enduring guarantees, recurring obligations or a broader family.

grounding.quote:
Acceptance exhausts only that instance and its
declared acceptance interval; it does not discharge an enduring guarantee,
a recurring obligation or a broader product family beyond the accepted
instance.

constraints.statement: Judge progress and supported-path promotion against the same selected outcome. Only material advance projects product progress; preservation is useful proof, prerequisite readiness stays bounded and names its enabled obligation, regression is not new progress. Acceptance stops that exact outcome instance selecting further progress; witnesses remain preservation/regression evidence. Later work is preservation, a bounded prerequisite for another admitted outcome or lawfully repriced change, never extra progress on the accepted instance. Selecting another already-defined unresolved outcome is goals/sequencing; changing meaning/scope or adding an outcome requires Product re-entry. Completing matrices, proofs, inventories, methods or tests cannot select/enlarge/replace an outcome. Explicitly product-defined assurance capability may be product progress, but evidence does not author the claim; one artifact's output/evidence roles must be separately declared.
constraints.uncertainty: ACTIVATION's unchanged churn and forecast-revision meanings are referenced but not supplied.

conditions: Material realisation growth within a product-outcome-bearing work wave.

grounding.quote:
Admission or renewal of a prerequisite or experiment belongs to the
authority owning the selected work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy,
and is recorded in the existing durable goals or ticket authority.

constraints.statement: Growth derives authority only from the selected unresolved outcome, an admitted named bounded prerequisite, or admitted named bounded experiment whose observation discriminates a stated decision for it. Prerequisite/experiment authorises only its provisional bound, neither changes outcome nor authorises downstream work, promotion or closure nor waives design/safety/authority/release law including applicable profile prime law. Owner or explicitly bounded proxy admits/renews, durably recording bound and exhaustion/falsification condition in goals/ticket authority. Satisfying decision-discriminating observation exhausts an experiment. Drafting/validating contracts or tickets, active status and prior admission create/extend/renew nothing. Acceptance, prerequisite discharge, experiment resolution, admitted terminal condition, rejection, withdrawal, supersession, repricing-away or evidential falsification ends the basis. Repair, continuation, evidence, run state and prior admission cannot renew ended authority; further material work requires new admission.

exceptions: Independent parallel work may proceed under its own admitted basis.

grounding.quote:
A regression or unresolved gap blocks further promotion on the affected
path until repaired, repriced or accepted by the owning authority.

constraints.statement: Retention as supported behaviour, required evidence, regression protection or bounded donor material confers no growth authority. Consumer owns deletion/archive/quarantine/salvage mechanics. Salvage carries only explicitly re-adopted semantics, inheriting no enclosing authority, dependencies, completion claim or work-selection power. Regression or unresolved gap blocks affected-path promotion until repaired, repriced or owner-accepted; it does not globally serialise independent admitted work, whose progress cannot be attributed to this outcome. Outcome success is necessary delivery evidence, not complete Product/release closure.

conditions: Every substantive change.

grounding.quote:
Every substantive change begins with intake triage, an explicit declared
change intent and a lawful re-entry point into the constitutional chain

constraints.statement: Every substantive change begins with intake triage, explicit declared change intent and a lawful constitutional-chain re-entry point.
